## Functional assignment

The 103-residue protein is most likely a **pyrimidine/purine nucleoside phosphorylase**.

This assignment is supported by:

- 60–64% identity to reviewed nucleoside phosphorylases across essentially the full sequence
- A strong **Ppnp domain** match, PF06865.18, spanning residues 12–102
- Agreement among multiple curated homolog annotations
- Predicted size of approximately **11.5 kDa**, consistent with this small phosphorylase family

## Catalytic activity

The enzyme catalyzes the reversible phosphorolysis of nucleosides:

\[
\text{Nucleoside} + \text{phosphate}
\rightleftharpoons
\text{free nucleobase} + \alpha\text{-D-ribose-1-phosphate}
\]

Representative reactions include:

\[
\text{Adenosine} + P_i
\rightleftharpoons
\text{Adenine} + \alpha\text{-D-ribose-1-phosphate}
\]

\[
\text{Guanosine} + P_i
\rightleftharpoons
\text{Guanine} + \alpha\text{-D-ribose-1-phosphate}
\]

\[
\text{Uridine} + P_i
\rightleftharpoons
\text{Uracil} + \alpha\text{-D-ribose-1-phosphate}
\]

Close reviewed homologs are annotated with **EC 2.4.2.1 and EC 2.4.2.2** and can act on several nucleosides, including adenosine, guanosine, inosine, cytidine, uridine, thymidine, and xanthosine. The exact substrate preference of this particular sequence cannot be established from homology alone.

## Summary

**Most likely function:** broad-specificity nucleoside phosphorylase involved in nucleoside salvage and/or degradation, producing free bases and ribose-1-phosphate. No specific cofactor requirement was identified.
